title: eIM: GPU-Accelerated Efficient Influence Maximization in Large-Scale Social Networks
problem: Influence maximization (IM) in large networks is NP-hard. State-of-the-art GPU IMM (Influence Maximization via Martingales) algorithm incurs significant memory overhead from storing random reverse reachable (RRR) sets, limiting scalability.
motivation: Social network analysis and information propagation modeling require efficient IM. GPU IMM implementations show promise but memory footprint limits applicability to largest networks.
method: eIM: GPU-accelerated IMM algorithm with optimized memory efficiency. Reduces RRR set storage requirements while maintaining algorithm correctness. Achieves similar accuracy to baselines with improved memory utilization.
key_novelty: Memory-efficient GPU IMM implementation; 1-3 orders of magnitude speedups over GPU baselines; 54% reduction in memory requirements for network data + RRR sets; scalability improvement through reduced memory footprint.
contributions: 1-3 orders of magnitude speedups over GPU implementations
54% memory reduction for network + RRR sets

metrics.speedup: 1-3 orders of magnitude vs. GPU baselines

limitations: Abstract-only evaluation; specific network sizes not mentioned; comparison to CPU implementations unclear; memory optimization technique not detailed
